boundary: Read-only official-document research and local source inspection. No developer app, credential, OAuth grant, account capability or live publishing action was performed.

input_contract.finalPreview: Selects only the latest tenant snapshot asset with role=render and mimeType=video/mp4; canExport requires timeline clips.

controls: Asset manifest/content access authorizes the actor against the project.
Rendered assets carry sha256 and inputDigest metadata and are durable across restart.
HTTP asset responses use bounded stored bytes and nosniff where applicable.
asset_contract.gap_for_OCP_03: The existing final preview identifies an MP4 but does not yet perform platform-specific codec, dimension, duration, frame/audio or metadata validation.

controls: Protected API calls authenticate an account and authorize project membership.
Cookie-authenticated mutations require a matching CSRF token.
Sessions rotate, expire and revoke; API keys are stored as hashes rather than reusable plaintext.
Project asset lookup rejects cross-project and cross-tenant access.

durability_contract.gap_for_OCP_04: Commercial job states are too coarse for remote upload, processing, publish and unknown-result reconciliation and must not be reused without the publishing-specific state contract.

regression_invariants: Beginner workbench remains the signed-in default and final preview/export remains available.
Advanced canvas and commercial-v2 generation remain reachable and unchanged.
Identity, tenant membership, CSRF, asset ownership, upload limits, credits and provider gates remain enforced.
Publishing code must consume an existing asset; it must not alter generation or charge inference credits.

platforms.official_flow: Query current creator info, initialize Direct Post, transfer bytes or use an ownership-verified URL, then reconcile publish_id via status polling/webhook.
eligibility_and_review: Unaudited clients are restricted to private visibility; audit is required to lift that restriction.
The product must meet Content Sharing Guidelines; an internal-only uploader for accounts managed by the developer/team is explicitly listed as unacceptable.
limits_and_semantics: creator_info is documented at 20 requests/minute per user token.
publish init is documented at 6 requests/minute per user token.
Posting and active-creator caps apply and may vary by account/client.
User must edit preset title/hashtags and expressly consent before transfer; processing can take minutes.
platforms.live_gate: Named TikTok developer app audit/scope approval, named account OAuth and named-asset Direct Post each require owner confirmation.

platforms.official_flow: Upload MP4 with /video/upload/ or documented multipart flow, obtain video_id, create with /video/create/, then query authorized video/status data where approved.
eligibility_and_review: video.create is documented as default-off, requiring management-console application and user authorization.
Additional delete, data, list, POI and other scopes are not required for basic creation and must not be requested unless a separately accepted feature needs them.
limits_and_semantics: Official upload documentation recommends MP4/WebM and states duration up to 15 minutes.
Single upload is documented up to 128 MB; above 128 MB requires multipart and the documented total maximum is 4 GB.
Content undergoes the same review logic as first-party uploads; watermark/logo policy can reduce distribution or cause removal/account action.
platforms.live_gate: Named Douyin developer app video.create approval, named account OAuth and named-asset creation each require owner confirmation.

platforms.official_flow: For an eligible Instagram professional account, create a REELS media container, transfer or expose the video through the documented upload mode, poll status_code, call media_publish, then retain the returned media id.
eligibility_and_review: Content Publishing supports Instagram professional accounts, not consumer accounts.
The Facebook Login path requires the connected Page/account relationship; extra ads scopes are conditional on the documented Business Manager role case and are not default scopes.
limits_and_semantics: The official guide exposes media, media_publish, status_code and content_publishing_limit operations.
The current official guide documents 100 API-published posts per moving 24-hour period.
URL transfer requires media reachable by Meta; resumable video upload is available only on the documented Facebook Login for Business path.
platforms.live_gate: Named Meta app advanced access/review where required, named professional account OAuth and named-asset media_publish each require owner confirmation.

platforms.official_flow: Upload through YouTube Data API videos.insert, preferably with the resumable upload protocol, then reconcile the returned video resource and processing/status fields.
eligibility_and_review: There is no separate Shorts publishing endpoint; qualifying uploaded videos are classified by YouTube product rules.
Videos uploaded by API projects created after 28 July 2020 that have not passed audit are restricted to private viewing until the project passes audit.
limits_and_semantics: videos.insert requires OAuth authorization and consumes API quota; quota exhaustion must be treated as a non-blind-retry condition.
Resumable upload is the required recovery design for interrupted transfers.
The UI must collect and preserve required child-directed/audience declarations and selected privacy rather than infer them silently.
platforms.live_gate: Named Google Cloud project/API audit or quota approval, named channel OAuth and named-asset videos.insert each require owner confirmation.

rules: Account-derived values override static documentation when they are more restrictive.
Missing, expired or contradictory capability data fails closed before upload.
Static limits are versioned evidence, never an authorization to publish.
The user sees the destination identity, selected privacy and any platform-specific adaptation before final confirmation.

threat_model.threat: OAuth login CSRF, callback injection or code replay
controls: bind state to tenant, actor, platform and intended return path

threat_model.threat: Credential theft from browser, logs, database or backups
controls: envelope encryption with separated key material
authorize project and account ownership server-side
bind asset digest and account to intent
opaque identifiers do not grant access
no silent privacy or audience change
only issue signed bounded asset URLs to allowlisted official origins
bind remote id to tenant intent
polling reconciliation remains authoritative when signatures are unavailable

threat_model.threat: Retry storms, quota abuse or worker crash

deferred_human_gates: Per-platform developer application or publishing-scope application/approval
Any platform credential addition, replacement or rotation
